summary.headline: CMR Green's AGM: FY26 revenue rose 29.5% to ₹8,640 crore and EBITDA 50.4% to ₹449.4 crore; ₹200 crore capex under way for two new plants.
summary.overview: This was the first AGM since listing, held by video conferencing on 29 September 2026, with the Chairman and Managing Director excused for a medical emergency, so Whole-time Director Akshay Agarwal chaired. Management reported FY26 sales volume up about 24% to 409,000 MT, EBITDA margin of about 5.2% (from 4.5%) and PAT up 47.3% to ₹228.4 crore. In Q&A, management said the West Asia conflict disrupted scrap routing and lifted prices, but margins were stated to be hedged, so gains were operational rather than windfall. Management also outlined a ₹200 crore capex programme with two new plants and brownfield expansions targeting 6-7 lakh tonnes of capacity by end of the calendar year.

financial_highlights.value: ~₹12.5/kg in Q1 after West Asia war

segments.name: Aluminium recycling (aluminium alloys, billets, wrought alloys, green aluminium)
segments.commentary: Aluminium volume grew ~27% in FY26; company is moving beyond cast alloys into billets, wrought alloys and green aluminium. Serves automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers.

segments.name: Non-aluminium (zinc alloys and other recycled metals)
segments.commentary: Non-aluminium sales volume grew ~18% in FY26. Company is evaluating copper, lead and lithium-ion battery recycling.

segments.name: Carbon credits (by-product of molten metal supply)
segments.commentary: Generates ~50,000-60,000 tCO2 savings units a year; accumulated over 270,000 carbon credits to date.

guidance_outlook: Capacity to reach 6-7 lakh tonnes per annum by end of the current calendar year, through two new plants plus brownfield expansion at four existing plants.
Management expects aluminium demand CAGR of about 11-13% in coming years, citing EVs, solar panels, packaging and auto.
Company intends to keep margins hedged and prioritise consistent profitability over windfall gains from metal price spikes.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 615,000 tpa across 13 recycling facilities in 8 states as of 31 March 2026.
₹200 crore capex committed for the year; about ₹53 crore spent in Q1.
Two new plants under construction this year: Shoolagiri and Bawal, aimed at EV and auto aluminium demand.
Brownfield expansions underway at four existing plants.
Installed solar capacity about 9.55 MW across facilities.
demand_pricing: Management said West Asia conflict rerouted scrap shipments away from the Suez Canal and through Strait of Hormuz transshipment ports, causing sudden scrap shortages and sharp price increases.
Company said it gained market share during the disruption by serving customers others could not.
Management stated margin gains were driven by operational efficiency and economies of scale, not windfall, because the company is hedged.
Low per-capita aluminium consumption in India cited as a structural growth driver.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current scrap processing and recycling capacity, and what is the plan to add capacity over the next two to three years from IPO proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshay Agarwal said two plants are being added this year at Shoolagiri and Bawal, with ₹200 crore capex committed (₹53 crore spent in Q1), plus brownfield expansions at four existing plants to reach 6-7 lakh tonnes by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the recent West Asia war on operations and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scrap shortages and price spikes followed rerouting via the Suez Canal and Hormuz ports; the company grew market share, and per-tonne margin rose from ~₹11.5 to ~₹12.5 in Q1, but this was attributed to efficiency and scale because the company is hedged.

qa_highlights.question: What steps is the company taking to reduce its carbon footprint?
qa_highlights.answer: Company earns carbon credits from molten metal supply (50,000-60,000 units a year, over 270,000 cumulative), is cutting Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions, shifting from diesel to CNG, using electricity and EVs in internal fleets, and expanding solar.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth plans after listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited aluminium demand CAGR of 11-13% from EVs, solar, packaging and autos; plans include new products, capacity growth in existing lines and higher market share.

risks_watch: Scrap availability and pricing volatility from geopolitical disruption (West Asia conflict, shipping routes).
Execution risk on Shoolagiri and Bawal plants and brownfield expansions to reach 6-7 lakh tpa by year-end.
Thin EBITDA margin (~5.2%) and PAT margin (~2.64%); sustainability of per-tonne margin gains after hedging.
Shares reported trading below the IPO issue price (per a retail shareholder), a sentiment factor.
Pipeline of new businesses (copper, lead, lithium-ion battery recycling) is at evaluation stage only.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and capacity growth, with the speaker stressing consistency and hedging. Evasive on specifics: no quantified Q1 FY27 revenue, volume or capex guidance beyond ₹53 crore spent, and no quantified hedging or carbon-reduction targets.
key_quotes: We were, in fact, able to grow our market share during this time because jo doosre log service nahin kar paaye, woh hum log kar paaye.

So while we did increase our margin from about eleven and a half odd rupees in the last year to about twelve and a half rupees in the first quarter after the West Asia war, but it was largely driven by operational efficiency, economies of scale rather than a windfall profit because we are hedged.

adds.what: Two new plants (Shoolagiri and Bawal) plus brownfield expansions at four existing plants, taking capacity to 6-7 lakh tpa

growth.why: Management guides installed capacity to 6-7 lakh tpa by end of calendar 2026 from 615,000 tpa, backed by a ₹200 crore capex programme (about ₹53 crore spent in Q1) for Shoolagiri and Bawal plants and four brownfield expansions, with no per-plant numbers given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to ~5.2% from 4.5% in FY25 and per-tonne margin ~₹12.5/kg in Q1 vs ~₹11.5 prior year, but management says it is hedged and prioritises consistency over windfall, so expansion is not guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Capacity of 615,000 tpa is to reach 6-7 lakh tpa by end of calendar 2026 via Shoolagiri and Bawal plants plus brownfield at four sites, with ₹200 crore committed and ~₹53 crore spent in Q1.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 volume rose ~24% to 409,000 MT, management cites 11-13% aluminium demand CAGR and gained share during the scrap disruption, though no Q1 FY27 volume was quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of ₹200 crore is already committed for FY27, and the capacity build-out is tied to 6-7 lakh tpa; the call gave no further plant plan or board approval beyond this, so a fresh programme is conditional on the current build-out.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue, volume or margin guidance was quantified for FY27 and management was evasive on Q1 FY27 numbers beyond capex spend.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Execution risk on Shoolagiri, Bawal and four brownfield expansions to reach 6-7 lakh tpa by year-end, plus scrap price volatility from the West Asia disruption on a thin ~5.2% EBITDA margin.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Company is moving into billets, wrought alloys and green aluminium, but no launch dates were given and copper, lead and lithium-ion battery recycling are only at evaluation stage.

rows.label: Share gains during scrap disruption
rows.why: Management said it gained market share by serving customers others could not during the West Asia scrap shortage, but no order or share figures were quantified.

rows.label: Carbon credit income
rows.why: Carbon credits of 50,000-60,000 units a year, with over 270,000 accumulated, give a recurring by-product income stream tied to molten metal supply.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 results (PAT up 47.3% to ₹228.4 crore) and the ₹200 crore capacity build-out, stressing hedging and consistency, but was evasive on Q1 FY27 numbers, hedging and carbon targets; the Q&A covered capacity, the West Asia impact, carbon footprint and growth plans.
